item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Tshisekedi unveiled a government composition including Judith Suminwa as Prime Minister and 54 ministers; she was described as the first woman to head the DRC.","notes":["The excerpt says he unveiled the composition of the government, not explicitly that he formed it."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The new government comprised 55% neophytes, including in key posts such as interior, defence and foreign affairs; some appointees from Tshisekedi’s UDPS party were occupying ministerial posts for the first time.","notes":["The excerpt does not state that 55% were first-time ministers; it states 55% were neophytes and separately that some appointees were in ministerial posts for the first time."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The source says Tshisekedi’s decision to appoint UDPS loyalists and technocrats aimed to ensure a more fluid government operation by insulating ministers from political dynamics.","notes":["Narrowed “promote” to the excerpt’s stated aim to ensure a more fluid operation; no achieved effect is established."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The source identifies a confrontation between Tshisekedi’s presidentialist leanings and the constitution’s semi-presidential structure with parliamentary checks, and notes that elected representatives of Maniema Province objected to their absence from the new government team.","notes":["The excerpt does not explicitly state that the approach could concentrate power despite the checks; it describes a constitutional tension and a possible move toward a majority-based system."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0012-R11-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The report says Tshisekedi’s administration continued to confront violence by armed groups and neighbouring countries in eastern DRC, while Rwandan-backed M23 was extending its hold in North Kivu.","notes":["The excerpt does not establish that armed groups generally continued to control territory; it specifically describes M23 extending its hold in North Kivu."]}]}
